stem:
A student investigates how the volume of a gas varies with its temperature. Air is trapped in a transparent cylinder of diameter *d* with a movable piston as shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The distance between the base of the cylinder and the bottom of the piston is *h*.

The trapped air is heated by placing the cylinder in water of temperature *θ*. The increase in temperature of the trapped air causes the piston to move. When the piston stops moving, the value of *h* is measured.

For each value of *h*, the volume *V* of the trapped air is calculated.

The experiment is repeated for different values of *θ*.

It is suggested that *V* and *θ* are related by the equation

*pV* = γκ(*θ* + *Z*)

where κ is the Boltzmann constant, *p* is the atmospheric pressure, and γ and *Z* are constants.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph is plotted of *V* on the y-axis against *θ* on the x-axis.

Determine expressions for the gradient and y-intercept.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Values of *θ* and *h* are given in Table 2.1.

[[fig:f2]]

The value of *d* is (27.9 ± 0.1) mm.
The volume *V* is calculated using the relationship

*V* = π*d*²*h*/4.

Calculate and record values of *V* / 10⁻⁵ m³ in Table 2.1. Include the absolute uncertainties in *V*.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Plot a graph of *V* / 10⁻⁵ m³ against *θ* / °C. Include error bars for *V*.

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable straight line on your graph. Label both lines.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the gradient of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Determine the y-intercept of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
Using your answers to (a), (c)(iii) and (c)(iv), determine the values of γ and *Z*. Include appropriate units.

Data: *p* = (1.01 ± 0.01) × 10⁵ Pa
κ = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the percentage uncertainty in γ.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: The experiment is repeated. Determine the temperature *θ* that gives a value of *h* of 60.0 mm.
